The 6 modules are NOT counted as applications; they are internal units of one application, and every app_1/app_2/applications[] value below is deliberately written as '<application_id>/<module_id>' so an internal unit can never be mistaken for a wave application id. The application itself is fully covered by this artifact at module grain, so coverage_exclusions is empty and omitted. COMPARED UNITS (6): form1-dashboard, insert-form, edit-form, view-form, module1-db-connection, my-project-infrastructure - taken verbatim from discovery/c70846ac-0948-4953-990c-c68a2be292d9/structural-analysis.json modules[].id. METHOD: all 15 unordered module pairs were scored sequentially (no fan-out: 6 units / 15 pairs is below the skill's fan-out threshold, and the 3 staged Discovery artifacts are the dominant input), using the three prescribed lenses. entity_overlap = Jaccard over the set of students-table columns each module actually references. operation_overlap = Jaccard over the set of named operations each module implements. persona_overlap = 100 where two modules serve the same human persona, 0 where they do not (the application has exactly one undifferentiated unauthenticated operator persona covering all four forms; module1-db-connection and my-project-infrastructure have zero human-facing surface and serve only the developer/maintainer persona). technology_overlap = 100 for every pair, because all 6 modules are Visual Basic .NET / WinForms / .NET Framework 4.8 inside a single assembly - it is a real property of a single-assembly monolith and it is weighted low precisely so it cannot manufacture a cluster on its own. COMPOSITE = 0.35*entity + 0.35*operation + 0.20*persona + 0.10*technology; cluster threshold 60. data_sot_conflicts.app_a_definition: A closed three-value domain - Male, Female, Other - declared as Designer Items literals and written to the column verbatim. edit-form declares the identical three-value domain.
data_sot_conflicts.app_b_definition: A two-value domain - Male, Female - restated independently as SQL literals in two COUNT(*) queries, with no 'Other' bucket and no grand total anywhere on the dashboard.
data_sot_conflicts.recommended_sot: Neither. Promote the domain out of both modules into one enumeration owned by the student-record service (and ideally a database check constraint), then derive both the entry-form dropdowns and the dashboard census from it. A student stored as 'Other' is currently storable, listable and editable but counted in no statistic, and because no total is displayed the shortfall is invisible - so picking either existing module as source of truth preserves the defect in one direction or the other.

data_sot_conflicts.app_a_definition: A closed, already-expired list of five string literals 2019-2023 declared in the Designer Items collection (duplicated identically in edit-form).
data_sot_conflicts.app_b_definition: Five buckets derived arithmetically by subtracting 0-4 from a local variable hardcoded to the literal 2023, with no reference to the system clock, then concatenated back into a quoted string to match the TEXT column lexically.
data_sot_conflicts.recommended_sot: Neither. The two halves agree only by coincidence of literals and both are already wrong: every academic-year tile has been incorrect since 1 January 2024, and extending the dropdown to 2024 without editing the constant would place new students in no cohort tile at all. The cohort definition must be restated as a requirement with stakeholders and then owned in one place - the current SQL and the current dropdown are both evidence of intent, not a specification.

data_sot_conflicts.entity: students.RollNo (mutability of the de-facto primary key)
data_sot_conflicts.app_a_definition: Freely user-typed: no mask, no length limit, no format or check-digit rule, no generation scheme, and no duplicate pre-check before the INSERT.
data_sot_conflicts.app_b_definition: Immutable: the same logical field is ReadOnly in the Designer and rollno appears only in the UPDATE WHERE clause, never in the SET list.
data_sot_conflicts.recommended_sot: edit-form's immutability answer, made explicit. Treat RollNo as an immutable key enforced by a declared unique index (no primary key or unique index was found in the decoded .accdb, so uniqueness is currently assumed by the code and enforced nowhere), and add the duplicate pre-check insert-form lacks. Re-keying a student is today possible only by delete-and-recreate, which is non-atomic and unaudited. Confirm against a live Access engine before migrating - the upstream decode could not resolve index definitions.

consolidation_candidates.group_name: Student record CRUD - three screens, one capability
consolidation_candidates.shared_capability: Create, read, search, update and delete the student record (the single ten-column students table) - the one genuine business capability in the application
consolidation_candidates.rationale: Seeded by the above-threshold pair insert-form <-> edit-form (composite 85) and grown by the clique rule: every internal pair clears the 60 threshold (insert/edit 85, edit/view 78, insert/view 74), all three modules reference all ten columns of the same students table, all three address single rows through the same rollno key, and all three serve the same single unauthenticated operator persona. The duplication is not incidental - insert-form and edit-form are parallel implementations of one ten-field record editor with byte-for-byte identical 24-control Designer layouts (373 vs 371 lines) and the field-to-parameter mapping written twice, and view-form independently triplicates its own grid-population logic across LoadData, LoadSData and RefreshData. ANCHOR CHOICE (contested - see the canonical-target-contested review ask): edit-form is proposed because it is the only module that already implements both the read and the write of the complete ten-field record, it is the only one with a real constructor contract, both its statements are parameterized, and it carries the lowest technical-debt band of the three (medium, versus insert-form medium-high and view-form high). view-form is explicitly NOT the anchor despite having the strongest incoming call edges, because it holds the application's only confirmed SQL-injection vector and is the module that unilaterally closes the shared global connection. PREREQUISITES, not side effects: this cluster cannot be collapsed before the shared global OleDbConnection is replaced with connection-per-operation plus real transactions, rollno is declared as an enforced unique key, the search predicate is reparameterized, and field validation is written for the first time (the create path has none at all). Those are new work, not ported work. RECOMMENDATION RATIONALE: shared_service rather than merge, because the right target is one student-record service owning all data access (all 16 SQL statements currently live in UI event handlers; the nominal data-access module holds 13 lines and zero queries) with the two editor layouts collapsed into a single record-editor component behind it. Structural analysis independently proposes the same boundary under the name student-record-crud-service.

rejected_from_cluster.reason: Failed the clique rule against all three members (composites 46, 46, 51 - every one below the 60 threshold) and does not share the cluster's primary capability: it implements read-only aggregate statistics, navigation and child-form hosting, referencing only 3 of the 10 students columns and never a single row. The shared-identifier growth rule does not rescue it either: form1-dashboard never references rollno, the cluster's primary key, and its overlap with the cluster on the Gender and YOA value domains is a CONFLICT (two-value versus three-value Gender domain; hardcoded-2023 arithmetic versus a fixed 2019-2023 list) rather than a delta, which that rule explicitly excludes. Recorded instead as a separate read-model concern and as three data_sot_conflicts entries. Note that structural analysis assigns form1-dashboard its own boundary, student-statistics-read-model, which agrees with this rejection.

Failed the clique rule against all three members (composite 18 against each). It duplicates nothing: 13 lines, zero SQL statements, zero students column references, and a single operation (open the shared connection). Its relationship to the cluster is shared mutable state to be CUT, not redundant function to be consolidated - which is the opposite of a consolidation signal and must not be read as one. The shared-identifier rule does not apply because module1-db-connection never references rollno. It is excluded here even though structural analysis lists it inside the student-record-crud-service boundary, because that listing is a statement about where the future data-access layer belongs, not evidence that this module duplicates a capability today. Replacing it remains a hard prerequisite for collapsing the cluster.

Failed the clique rule against all three members (composite 10 against each) on every lens that carries redundancy signal: zero entity overlap (db_access 'none'), zero operation overlap, zero shared human persona. It is entirely Designer-generated application plumbing. It is named here only because its generated My.Forms default-instance collection is the mechanism that makes the cluster's cross-module refresh calls compile - a dependency to re-specify during consolidation, not a member to absorb.

review_asks.title: Which part of the Student Management System should become the single student-record component the others fold into?
review_asks.why: Consolidation sequencing, effort estimates and every downstream disposition hang on which component survives, and the two candidates fail in opposite directions - so picking wrongly either preserves a defect or silently expands the scope of work.

subject.label: Student Management System (VB.NET) - cluster smsvb-student-record-crud (cluster address module: c70846ac-0948-4953-990c-c68a2be292d9/edit-form)

confidence.rationale: The cluster itself is high-confidence - every internal pair clears the threshold on strong evidence. The anchor choice is not: edit-form wins on debt and completeness, insert-form wins on being the only component that can write the record key, and neither covers list, search or delete. That is a genuine trade-off, not a measurement.

review_asks.assessment: SUBJECT NOTE FIRST: this ask is about the three-module cluster smsvb-student-record-crud, not about any one module. It is addressed at the application id because that is the only durable identifier in scope that does not move when the proposed anchor changes - the skill's rule is to address a cluster through a member that cannot shift, and in an intra-app artifact the internal unit ids are not application ids and would not resolve downstream. Naming edit-form in the label above is an address, not an endorsement. THE ASSESSMENT: three of the six modules - insert-form, edit-form and view-form - implement one capability, create/read/search/update/delete of the single ten-column student record. Their duplication is measured, not inferred: all three reference all ten columns, all three key on the same roll number, and insert-form and edit-form are two builds of the same data-entry screen with identical 24-control layouts and the ten-field mapping written twice. We propose edit-form as the component to keep and fold the other two into, but we are flagging the choice rather than making it, because the strongest objection is substantive: edit-form is the only one of the three that CANNOT write the roll number at all (the field is deliberately read-only there), so anchoring on it means adding a capability insert-form already has.
review_asks.reasoning: Scored all 15 module pairs on entity overlap, operation overlap, persona and technology. Signals favouring edit-form: lowest technical-debt band of the three (medium, versus insert-form medium-high and view-form high); the only module implementing BOTH the read and the write of the complete ten-field record; both its statements parameterized; the only module with a real constructor contract rather than a VB default instance. Signals favouring insert-form: it owns the complete ten-column write including the roll number, which edit-form cannot write; and it is the only module whose every statement is a single clean parameterized INSERT. Signals that conflicted and ruled view-form out despite it having the strongest incoming call edges: it holds the application's only confirmed SQL-injection vector and it is the module that unilaterally closes the application-wide database connection. A third reading is defensible and is offered as an option: upstream structural analysis recommends a NEW student-record-crud-service boundary rather than promoting any existing form, on the grounds that all 16 SQL statements currently sit in UI event handlers and the nominal data-access module holds 13 lines and no queries - so on that view there is no existing component clean enough to anchor, and the real work is creating the layer rather than choosing among the three screens. Whichever option is chosen, the same prerequisites apply first: replace the shared global connection, declare the roll number as an enforced unique key, reparameterize the search, and write field validation that does not exist today.

review_asks.why: This duplication is invisible in the portfolio-wide comparison, it changes the refactor estimate for this application, and three of the disagreements are producing wrong output or data loss today rather than merely costing maintenance effort.

confidence.rationale: Every claim rests on named file-and-line evidence from two independent upstream passes that corroborate each other: identical control counts in the two editor layouts, the ten-field mapping written twice, and three value-domain declarations that do not agree.

review_asks.assessment: The add, edit and list screens are three implementations of one job - creating, finding, changing and deleting the student record - over one ten-column table. The add and edit screens are effectively the same screen built twice: identical 24-control layouts and the same ten-field mapping written out twice, so any change to a field rule has to be made in two places. Separately, the list screen contains three different routines that all fill the same grid, and only one of them is exposed to the injection flaw. Three disagreements between the duplicated copies are worth investigating as business questions, not just code cleanup. (1) The add and edit screens offer three gender values but the dashboard counts only two, so any student recorded as 'Other' appears in no statistic and the tiles do not add up to the student population - and no total is shown anywhere that would reveal the gap. (2) The admission-year list on the entry screens stops at 2023 and the dashboard's year tiles are computed from a hardcoded 2023, so every year tile has been wrong since January 2024 and the error grows by one year annually with no warning. (3) The roll number can be freely typed when adding a student but cannot be changed when editing one, so correcting a mistyped roll number requires deleting and re-creating the record, with no audit trail and no safety net.
review_asks.reasoning: Compared all 6 internal modules pairwise on three lenses - which business entities each one handles, which operations each one performs, and which human role uses it. Three modules clustered: all three handle all ten columns of the same table, all three address single records by the same roll number, and all three are used by the same single operator (the application has no login, no roles and no separate read-only mode). The two remaining non-UI modules did not cluster and should not: the connection module duplicates nothing at all (13 lines, no queries), and the generated plumbing module has no data or user surface. The dashboard module also did not cluster - it reads only 3 of the 10 columns and never a single record - but it is where the three disagreements surface, because it restates the gender, course and year value lists independently instead of sharing them. One signal conflicted and is worth stating: the course list (BCA, MCA, IIMCA) is repeated in at least eight places across three modules and happens to agree everywhere, so the agreement is maintained by coincidence; adding a fourth course would make its students countable nowhere and, because of a case-sensitivity difference between the screens and the database, potentially un-editable.

review_asks.title: Please confirm the dashboard screen should be treated as a separate concern rather than consolidated with the student list screen.
review_asks.why: This pair scored just under the consolidation threshold, so if the judgement is wrong the dashboard gets planned and funded as a separate component when it should have been absorbed - or vice versa.

subject.label: Student Management System (VB.NET) - pair form1-dashboard / view-form (pair address module: c70846ac-0948-4953-990c-c68a2be292d9/form1-dashboard)

confidence.rationale: The score sits at 51 against a 60 threshold - close enough that a different weighting of the duplicated child-form hosting code would move it across. The capability argument for keeping them separate is stronger than the score margin, but it rests on a judgement about intent that the code does not state.

review_asks.assessment: The dashboard screen and the student list screen scored 51 out of 100 on combined overlap, just below the 60 we require to call two parts of an application duplicates. We are reporting the pair but NOT recommending consolidation, and would like that confirmed. The two screens show the same student rows to the same person in two ways - counts on tiles, rows in a grid - and they do duplicate some real code: both independently implement the same logic for embedding a child screen inside the dashboard panel, and both build database queries by gluing text together rather than binding values. But the dashboard reads only 3 of the 10 columns of the student record and never reads an individual student, so we judge it a separate reporting concern that should be rebuilt as a read-only statistics view rather than folded into the record-management work. Two caveats a reviewer should weigh: the dashboard is also the navigation shell and the host for every other screen, so it cannot be cleanly separated at today's granularity - splitting its 1,211-line layout file is itself a work item - and the dashboard's own statistics definitions are not trustworthy as a specification, since the year tiles have been wrong since January 2024 and the gender tiles exclude one of the three values the system accepts.
review_asks.reasoning: Composite = 0.35 x entity overlap + 0.35 x operation overlap + 0.20 x persona + 0.10 x technology. For this pair: entity 30 (the dashboard touches only Gender, Course and YOA of the ten columns, against the list screen's SELECT * which exposes all ten), operation 30 (child-screen hosting implemented twice in both modules, two coexisting query-assembly conventions, and grid-refresh entry points declared in one and called from the other), persona 100 (one undifferentiated operator uses both - there is no login, no role and no read-only mode anywhere), technology 100 (same language, framework, runtime and assembly). That gives 10.5 + 10.5 + 20 + 10 = 51. The conflicting signals: the persona lens pushes this pair up hard and is the only reason it reaches 51 at all, while the entity lens - the one that actually distinguishes reporting from record management - puts it at 30. We let the capability test break the tie, which is also where upstream structural analysis lands: it assigns the dashboard its own student-statistics-read-model boundary and explicitly notes that the overlap between that boundary and the navigation shell is itself the finding.

review_asks.title: Internal duplication scan recorded for the Student Management System: 6 internal parts compared, 15 comparisons, one duplicate group found.
review_asks.why: So the record shows exactly what was and was not examined, and on what evidence, before any consolidation decision is taken on this application.

confidence.rationale: All three required upstream inputs were present and complete, and the two independent passes corroborate each other on the same file-and-line evidence. The reservation is that no source repository was read by this pass and no uniqueness index could be confirmed upstream.

review_asks.assessment: This application was examined on its own, part by part, for work that is done more than once inside it. All 6 internal parts were compared against each other - 15 comparisons in total, none skipped - and the application is fully covered by this record, so nothing is listed as unexamined. One duplicate group was found: the add, edit and list screens all manage the same student record and should become one component behind one shared service. Three parts were considered and ruled out, each with its score recorded: the dashboard (separate reporting concern), the database-connection module (duplicates nothing - 13 lines and no queries, but replacing it is a prerequisite for the consolidation) and the generated application plumbing (no data and no user surface). Three disagreements between duplicated copies of the same rule are recorded separately as source-of-truth conflicts: the gender values, the admission-year definition, and whether the roll number can be changed. Two things this record does NOT contain, stated so they are not mistaken for clean results: no comparison against other applications, because this was a single-application examination by design - that work is done separately at portfolio scale; and no regulatory consistency findings, because the upstream analysis traced none of this application's 60 business rules to any regulation. On that last point, the governing profile for this run is the FAA profile as declared, and the upstream analysis recorded - as its own finding, which we restate here only as context - that an aviation-regulator profile does not obviously fit an academic student-records desktop tool. That is a profile-assignment question for a reviewer, not a conclusion of this scan.
review_asks.reasoning: Scope was intra-app, so the unit of comparison is the application's internal modules, taken verbatim from the upstream structural map: form1-dashboard, insert-form, edit-form, view-form, module1-db-connection, my-project-infrastructure. The count of applications examined is reported as 1, which is the honest figure - the 6 internal modules are not applications and are deliberately not counted as such, and every comparison below is written with the application id prefixed so an internal part can never be mistaken for a separate application. Each pair was scored on business entities handled, operations performed, human role served, and technology, weighted 0.35 / 0.35 / 0.20 / 0.10; the technology lens is weighted low on purpose because all 6 parts share one language and one assembly and would otherwise make everything look like a duplicate of everything. Evidence came entirely from the three supplied upstream analyses - business rules, structural map, and quality/risk - which agree with each other on the same file-and-line citations. No source repository was read by this pass, so every figure is marked as derived from supplied analysis rather than from a tool run. Known gaps carried forward from upstream and not papered over: record counts and database column types were never resolved, and no unique index on the roll number could be confirmed, so the roll-number recommendation needs checking against a live database engine.
